To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the shape of CF depends on both chip length and chip duty and (2) the BEP for the same PG varies with the chip length and duty.
the BEP of a pulsed binary DS-UWB system in a Nakagami fading environment is a function of the product of the PG and the average SNR per bit.
the shape of CF depends on the chip length, chip-duty and PG, and the BEP is a function of the CF, and the BEPs obtained by exact analysis and SGA are different for low duty systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exact analysis of pulsed DS-UWB system in Nakagami fading channels.
the exact analysis of pulsed DS-UWB systems in multiple access environment with episodic transmission, where a closed form expression for the CF of the sum of random variables is derived.

the exact BEP analysis of pulsed DS-UWB multiple access systems in Nakagami fading channels and is the first to present an exact closed form solution for the CF and hence the BEP for any arbitrary pulse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SGA is accurate for high duty systems in both highly and lightly faded channels and for low duty systems only in highly faded channels.
the SGA is not a good approximation for DS-UWB systems with low duty and low PG.
the SGA can not be applied to DS-UWB multiple access systems without a thorough understanding of the underlying system parameters and fading environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for the same PG, the BEP is the same for all combinations of the chip length, chip-duty and fading severity, but it varies substantially with the combination for the same fading severity.

the BEP for DS-UWB systems with arbitrary pulse shape and arbitrary PG in Nakagami fading channels, can be obtained in closed form through a simple method and the SGA can be used with a good accuracy for highly faded channel.
the BEP of DS-UWB systems with episodic transmission in Nakagami fading channels depends considerably both on the chip length and the chip-duty, which should be considered in system design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SGA should not be used blindly and the exact BEP should be evaluated for a given system.
the BEP of DS-UWB systems is a function of both the fading parameter and the PG, and the fading parameter is not necessarily equal to the PG.
the BEP of a DS-UWB system depends not only on the PG, as it is commonly perceived, but on the chip length and duty cycle also.
